blocks.content: A ServiceAccount is an identity for Pods and processes to authenticate to the Kubernetes API, exactly the object type behind the service-account-token Secret type introduced in the Configuration module.
1. An Identity for Pods, Not Humans
blocks.text: 1. An Identity for Pods, Not Humans

blocks.content: Where human operators authenticate with their own user identities, a Pod that needs to call the Kubernetes API itself (a controller, an automation tool running in-cluster) authenticates using a ServiceAccount instead.

blocks.alt: A distinct kind of identity, built specifically for automated, in-cluster callers

blocks.content: If a Pod spec does not specify a ServiceAccount explicitly, it is automatically assigned the namespace's default ServiceAccount, every Pod has some ServiceAccount identity, whether you thought about it or not.

blocks.alt: A default identity assigned automatically, even without deliberate configuration

blocks.content:
spec:
  serviceAccountName: my-app-sa
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: myapp:1.0

code.content:

  serviceAccountName: my-app-sa
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: myapp:1.0

codes.yaml:
spec:
  serviceAccountName: my-app-sa
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: myapp:1.0

blocks.content: This is exactly the mechanism previewed in the Configuration module's Secret Types topic, a ServiceAccount's authentication token is automatically mounted into every Pod using it, ready for any code inside the Pod that needs to call the API.

blocks.alt: A token, automatically present, exactly as previewed in the Configuration module

blocks.content: 4. Used for Real, In-Cluster API Calls
blocks.text: 4. Used for Real, In-Cluster API Calls

blocks.content: This is not a theoretical mechanism, controllers and operators running as Pods inside the cluster (things that themselves create, watch, or modify other Kubernetes objects) authenticate to the API server using exactly this token.

blocks.alt: The real mechanism behind any Pod that itself needs to talk to the Kubernetes API

blocks.content: 5. RBAC Applies to Service Accounts Too
blocks.text: 5. RBAC Applies to Service Accounts Too

blocks.content: This ties directly back to the RBAC topic, a ServiceAccount is a legitimate subject for a RoleBinding, exactly like a human user or group, letting you grant a specific Pod exactly the API permissions it needs, and nothing more.

blocks.alt: The exact same permission system, applied to automated callers as much as humans

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: A ServiceAccount is an identity for Pods and automated processes, every Pod gets one automatically (the default), with its token auto-mounted for API calls.
RBAC rules bind to ServiceAccounts exactly like human users, letting you grant a specific Pod exactly the API access it needs, following least privilege.
